findings.text: The first paragraph says what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. A newcomer can say what it is and why it matters before scrolling.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The title and heading are about firstmate, a project the newcomer has probably never heard of, not about Athena. Someone arriving at Athena's home page may at first think they are on the wrong site.
The first section after the navigation is an error message. It undercuts the opening claim that Athena "records what each step cost", at exactly the point where a newcomer would look for proof.
findings.source: "Check it on a real job": "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The page promises request-to-commit, then shows a study of another project. It never says how studies relate to the `athena ask` workflow, so a newcomer may not see why this study shows the main use.
findings.source: "It is for people who want to give a lazy, one- or two-line request and get back a commit" vs "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project"

findings.text: Next steps are concrete and linked from the top: a clone command, prerequisites, `./setup.sh` and an example `athena ask "add a changelog"`. The page also warns that it acts on the current repository and that you press Enter to run it. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the "Next steps" section

findings.text: The prerequisites mention cargo but do not list a Rust toolchain, and they do not say whether setup.sh installs one. A newcomer without Rust may not know whether they need it first.
findings.source: Next steps: "a C linker (cc), which cargo needs to build Athena"

findings.text: This link sits in the header with no explanation. A newcomer is not an owner and has no proposals, so it adds confusion at the top of the page.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The firstmate study is long and dense, but it is organized for a stranger: a one-line definition, a glossary of first-use terms, a step-by-step walk through one task, and expert sections hidden by default. That makes Athena's 'explained, with every claim traced' promise visible.
findings.source: "Start here" / "Words used first" and "Show expert detail (core track is the default)"

findings.text: Several glossary entries admit that a term is undefined. This is honest, but newcomers get gaps where they expect definitions, and "captain call" matters to the Reopened state.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." (also durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake)
